selfConsumptionNote: Share of a no-battery system's output used in the home as it is produced (typically 30-50% for a system sized to annual use). Only matters where exports earn less than retail.

default.label: Net metering
default.note: Exported power is credited at or near the retail rate, usually netted monthly or annually.

CA.label: Net Billing Tariff ("NEM 3.0")
CA.note: Exports earn hourly avoided-cost values (roughly 5-8¢ on average, higher on summer evenings) plus a small adder that drops to 0.9¢ for 2026 PG&E interconnections. Most new California systems add a battery to shift exports into the evening.

AZ.label: Resource Comparison Proxy export rate
AZ.note: APS and UNS Electric pay about 5.5¢ per exported kWh for applications from September 1, 2026, locked for 10 years. SRP customers (much of metro Phoenix) are on SRP's own solar plans.

HI.label: Smart Export
HI.note: Hawaiian Electric's Smart Export pays for exports only between 4 p.m. and 9 a.m. (about 15¢ on O'ahu) and nothing from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., when panels export most. Nearly all new Hawaii systems include a battery; without one, exports are worth little.

UT.label: Rocky Mountain Power export credit (Schedule 137)
UT.note: Rocky Mountain Power credits exports at 4.855¢ (June-September) and 4.033¢ (October-May) from March 2026, updated each March.

ID.label: Idaho Power export credit rate
ID.note: Idaho Power's export credit varies by season and hour (highest on summer evenings, a few cents at midday); about 5¢ is our blended estimate for a typical rooftop system. Rates reset each June.

MI.label: Distributed generation inflow/outflow
MI.note: DTE and Consumers Energy bill all power drawn from the grid at retail and credit exported power at roughly the power-supply part of the rate, about half of retail.

IL.label: Supply-only net metering
IL.note: Systems interconnected from 2025 are credited for exports at the electricity supply rate (ComEd's 2025 average was about 8.3¢), not the full delivered rate. Illinois Shines renewable-energy-credit payments and utility inverter rebates can shorten payback considerably and are not included here.

IN.label: Excess distributed generation (EDG)
IN.note: Indiana utilities credit exports at 1.25 times their average wholesale energy price, about 3.5-4.5¢, updated each year.

KY.label: Net metering service (NMS-2)
KY.note: LG&E and KU credit exports at about 7.1¢ and 7.5¢ per kWh (March 2026 Kentucky PSC orders); other Kentucky utilities set their own rates.

GA.label: Georgia Power solar buyback
GA.note: Georgia Power nets instantly and credits exports at its 2026 solar avoided cost (3.22¢) plus a 4¢ renewable adder, 7.22¢ in total, reset each January.

AL.label: Avoided-cost purchase plus capacity reservation charge
AL.note: Alabama Power buys exports at avoided cost (about 3¢) and charges solar customers a capacity reservation fee of $5.41 per kW per month, upheld by a federal judge in March 2026. Co-op and TVA-area customers have different terms.

TN.label: TVA Dispersed Power Production
TN.note: Tennessee has no net metering; TVA buys exports through its Dispersed Power Production program at about 2-3¢ per kWh, and local power companies may add a monthly fee.

LA.label: Avoided-cost net billing
LA.note: Louisiana PSC rules since 2020 credit exports at the utility's avoided cost, about a quarter of retail. Entergy New Orleans customers may still have retail net metering.

AR.label: Net billing (Act 278)
AR.note: Systems installed after September 30, 2024 are credited for exports at the utility's avoided cost, typically under half of retail.

MS.label: Net renewable generation
MS.note: Mississippi credits exports at the utility's avoided cost plus a 2.5¢ adder, about 6¢ in total.

TX.label: Retail provider solar buyback plans
TX.note: Texas has no statewide net metering. In competitive areas the export credit depends on your retail plan: most buyback plans pay about 3-9¢, a few match retail. Austin Energy pays a 9.9¢ value-of-solar rate; CPS Energy about 3-4¢.

SD.label: Avoided-cost purchase
SD.note: South Dakota utilities mostly don't offer net metering and pay avoided cost for exports, about 2-4¢.

ND.label: Avoided-cost net metering
ND.note: North Dakota investor-owned utilities credit excess generation at avoided cost, far below retail.

NV.label: Net metering (Tier 4)
NV.note: NV Energy credits power you use within the month at retail and pays 75% of retail for surplus beyond that. Northern Nevada (Sierra Pacific) systems approved after October 2025 net every 15 minutes, which lowers savings somewhat.

VA.label: Net metering (Dominion NEM 2.0)
VA.note: Dominion's 2026 successor keeps annual netting at retail; only surplus left at the end of the year is paid 5.8¢.

OK.label: Net metering
OK.note: Oklahoma rules net usage within the billing cycle; utilities buy any surplus at avoided cost, so oversized systems earn little on the extra.

ca/los-angeles.label: LADWP net energy metering
ca/los-angeles.note: Los Angeles is served by LADWP, a city-owned utility outside the state's Net Billing Tariff; it still credits exported power at or near retail. LADWP's residential rates (about 25-28¢ in 2026) are lower than the state average, so we use 26¢ here.
